topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to histopathology practicals, and outlines the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor Virology, Proto-Oncogenes, and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the discovery of viral transformation, the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes captured by retroviruses, and the laboratory assays used to test transformed phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Classifications of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressor Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer genes and explore their molecular mechanisms and dosage effects using the G1/S cell cycle checkpoint and p53 as examples.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific defects in DNA damage repair, DNA replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep Tumor Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the sequential accumulation of genetic alterations and inherited germline mutations accelerates cancer development and shapes tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and Reading Recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests complementary reading, and previews the upcoming lecture.
